derivation.scope: Research-only correction design. No production source edits, real-data run, external solver, posterior, scientific acceptance, or proof-status promotion. Status fail refers to seed general-law adequacy, not completion of this analytic assignment.
derivation.notation: Let Y=(Y0,...,Ym), Yi in R^{di}, Y~N(mu,C), Cij=Cov(Yi,Yj), C PSD. Fixed Ki maps R^{d(i-1)} to R^{di}. For i=1,...,m, ri=Yi-Ki Y(i-1). Block row Hi has -Ki in column i-1 and I_di in column i; all other blocks vanish. R=HY, mR=Hmu, S=HCH^T.
derivation.joint_covariance: Sij=Cij-C(i,j-1) Kj^T-Ki C(i-1,j)+Ki C(i-1,j-1) Kj^T. In particular Sii=Cii+Ki C(i-1,i-1) Ki^T-C(i,i-1) Ki^T-Ki C(i-1,i). Every block, not just neighboring i,j, is needed unless a declared law supplies exact zeros. Even block-independent Yi yield S(i,i+1)=-Cii K(i+1)^T from the shared Yi; disjoint residuals are independent only when their covariance blocks vanish under joint Gaussianity.
derivation.short_gaussian_proof: For every deterministic t, t^T R=(H^T t)^T Y is univariate Gaussian with mean t^T Hmu and variance t^T HCH^T t. Thus R has the stated (possibly degenerate) multivariate Gaussian law. The four cross terms follow by bilinearity of covariance. PSD follows from v^T S v=(H^T v)^T C(H^T v)>=0.
derivation.centering: For a stated model theta, test z=R-H mu(theta), not R unless Hmu(theta)=0 is the explicitly stated null. The source residual target-K source is a contrast, not generally a zero-mean innovation. A global/local candidate may itself predict nonzero contrast means.
derivation.support: Let S=U_r Lambda_r U_r^T with strictly positive retained eigenvalues; r=rank(S), P=U_r U_r^T=S S^+. Exact support is mR+range(S). Require (I-P)z=0. On support, q=z^T S^+ z=||Lambda_r^(-1/2) U_r^T z||^2 ~ chi-square_r for the true fixed mean and known covariance. Off support, the model assigns probability zero regardless of q. For r=0, z=0 deterministically, q=0 but q/r is undefined. A nonzero z is incompatible. Do not replace missing covariance or feature inputs with zero; zero rank is a known deterministic law, unlike unavailable data.
derivation.singular_likelihood_caution: For fixed rank/support, Gaussian density with respect to the induced r-dimensional support measure uses (2pi)^(-r/2) pdet(S)^(-1/2) exp(-q/2) and a support restriction. If support or rank changes with theta, model comparison must handle the measures and constraints explicitly; comparing pseudodeterminant densities alone is insufficient. Invertible anchored coordinates preserve the probability law, but for singular laws their induced support-volume Jacobian need not be the ambient determinant.
derivation.numerics: Declare separate PSD validation, rank, and support tolerances on appropriately scaled/standardized quantities. Numerical rank thresholds are an approximation policy, not proof of deterministic zeros. Reject materially negative eigenvalues. Record sensitivity near the cutoff. Do not clamp a genuinely indefinite quadratic to zero or silently jitter deterministic support into full rank. Known singular but support-valid is distinct from input unavailable and from support violation.
derivation.fixed_transport_vs_innovation: Geometric/feature Ki is fixed independently of the realization; it need not equal a regression coefficient and produces correlated contrasts. Gaussian sequential innovations instead use the entire past X_i=(Y0,...,Y(i-1)): ei=Yi-mui-C(i,past) C(past,past)^+ (X_i-mu_past). The conditional covariance is Vi=Cii-C(i,past) C(past,past)^+ C(past,i). Because a PSD block covariance implies ker(Cpast) subset ker(C(i,past)), the conditional mean is well-defined on the realized past support and Cov(ei,X_i)=0. Joint Gaussianity gives independence of ei from the full past and hence mutually independent innovations, including initial centered block. Degenerate Vi require support constraints. Regression on only Yi-1 gives innovations relative to the full past only if the corresponding Gaussian conditional Markov property is justified. Metadata nesting proves none of this.
derivation.innovation_counterexample: Take scalar three-depth covariance with all diagonal entries 1 and off-diagonals 1/2. Adjacent regressions use K=1/2. For e1=Y1-Y0/2 and e2=Y2-Y1/2, Cov(e1,e2)=1/2-1/2-1/4+1/8=-1/8, so they are not independent innovations. Regression of Y2 on (Y0,Y1) has coefficients (1/3,1/3) and innovation variance 2/3, with covariance zero against the whole past.
derivation.contrast_kernel_and_recovery: H has full row rank: given any contrasts and any Y0, recursively set Yi=ri+Ki Y(i-1). Its kernel consists of (v,K1 v,K2 K1 v,...,Km...K1 v), dimension d0. For Ki=I this is the constant mode. For arbitrary Ki, a literally constant vector is removed only if every Ki preserves that vector; the general loss is a transported-level mode. The square map A:Y -> (Y0,HY) is block lower triangular with identity diagonal and determinant 1, hence invertible without requiring any Ki inverse. Preserve full covariance ACA^T, whose initial-contrast blocks are Cov(Y0,ri)=C(0,i)-C(0,i-1)Ki^T, along with means and support. Replacing contrasts by scores or retaining only their marginal covariances destroys this recovery.
derivation.statistical_information_qualification: A noninjective data transformation loses sample coordinates but need not lose information about every chosen parameter. With C fixed SPD and Gaussian mean direction d, contrast Fisher information is d^T H^T(HCH^T)^(-1)H d <= d^T C^(-1)d. Whitening makes this an orthogonal-projection inequality. Equality holds precisely when C^(-1)d lies in range(H^T). For d in ker(H), contrast mean information vanishes. If covariance varies with theta, contrast covariance may still inform theta; the common-mean counterexample assumes fixed C. On singular known support, H can be injective on range(C) even though not globally injective, so avoid saying all contrasts necessarily lose stochastic information.
dependency_conditions: C must be a joint law for the exact same stacked estimators: shared objects, weights, masks, selections, calibration fits, reference subtraction and overlap induce cross-covariance. Marginal covariance IDs alone do not determine Cij.

If Ki is externally fixed, the linear Gaussian derivation applies. If a random Ki is independent of Y, conditioning on Ki preserves the specified Gaussian Y law; unconditional residual law can be a Gaussian mixture. If Ki is fitted from Y, H(Y)Y is generally nonlinear and neither Gaussianity nor H(Y) C H(Y)^T as its unconditional covariance follows. Conditioning on such a fitted Ki need not restore the original Gaussian law.

A fitted mean, covariance, transport, selection cut or nuisance projection needs the joint estimator law or a matched end-to-end repeated-sampling procedure. Plug-in chi-square calibration is not exact merely because the observed covariance is PSD. Independent training/cross-fitting helps isolate dependence but still requires conditioning and covariance estimation uncertainty to be specified.

For illustration of data-fit failure, choose scalar Khat=Y1/Y0 on Y0!=0. Then residual Y1-Khat Y0 is identically zero while treating the fitted Khat as fixed in an independent-unit covariance formula yields 1+Khat^2>0.

A valid Gaussian calibration is pointwise in a fixed true theta with known C. Fitting theta to the same data changes the residual law/degrees of freedom; nonlinear fitted models require explicit calibration. Nesting does not establish independent increments, exchangeability, Gaussianity or conditional sufficiency.

hand_controls.name: independent three-depth positive law
hand_controls.details: Eigenvalues 1,3. q(1,1)=2; q(1,-1)=2/3. Under this true law q~chi-square_2. Diagonal-only qD=(r1^2+r2^2)/2 has law (1/2)Z1^2+(3/2)Z2^2, expectation 2 but variance 5 rather than chi-square_2 variance 4. Matching expected score therefore does not validate its tail.

hand_controls.name: two-depth cross term controls
hand_controls.details: Ignoring covariance always gives variance 2. For zero mean, naive q=r^2/2 has law (1-rho) chi-square_1; rho=0.8 under-rejects and rho=-0.8 over-rejects a nominal upper-tail chi-square test.

hand_controls.name: duplicate observations
hand_controls.details: Y=mu+Z(1,1,1), so R=Hmu deterministically. Under common mean, R=(0,0); R=(1,0) violates support. A bare pseudoinverse reports q=0 in both cases. The source marginal-sum construction falsely uses per-edge variance 2.

hand_controls.name: constant mean removed and restored
hand_controls.details: Contrast law is independent of theta. In anchored coordinates the mean is (theta,0,0) and the full covariance is essential. theta_hat=Y0+(2 r1+r2)/3=(Y0+Y1+Y2)/3 has variance 1/3; using only Y0 has variance 1. Conditioning Y0 on contrasts gives variance 1/3 and a contrast-dependent conditional mean.

hand_controls.name: singular support distinction
hand_controls.details: z=(2,0): q=4, rank=1, valid support. z=(0,1): pseudoinverse q=0, invalid support. Zero covariance is legitimate only with exactly known deterministic constraints.
